page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the c3d family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor using x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16), AES cryptography, and SHA extensions.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is also a limiting factor, with cached and uncached read and write operations scoring in the bottom 25%. The server demonstrates average performance in single-threaded compression, text processing, and Passmark CPU encryption tests.

Given the hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance presents a clear tradeoff between strong single-threaded execution and constrained multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput. It is not optimized for memory-intensive operations, database tasks, or large language model inference, where it registers poor to weak performance. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving that do not require high memory bandwidth or local storage.
